title: Unbounded left derivability from a bounded-above resolving class
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive right exact functor, where right exact means preserving finite colimits. Let $\mathcal P\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal A)$ contain $0$, be closed under finite direct sums, and have every object of $\mathcal A$ as an epimorphic image of an object of $\mathcal P$. Assume that $F(P^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every bounded above acyclic cochain complex $P^\bullet$ whose terms belong to $\mathcal P$. Assume also that both categories admit colimits of diagrams indexed by $\mathbf N$ with its usual order [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], these sequential colimits preserve short exact sequences of diagrams, and $F$ commutes with them. Then the left derived functor of $Q_{\mathcal B}\circ K(F):K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is defined at every object in the sense of Situation 05S8 and Definition 05S9 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]; here $K(F)$ applies $F$ termwise to complexes and homotopy classes of chain maps, and $Q_{\mathcal B}:K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $\overline{\mathcal P}=\{M\cong P:P\in\mathcal P\}$. Let $\mathcal R$ consist of complexes $X$ presented as termwise sequential colimits of bounded above $\overline{\mathcal P}$-complexes $E_n$, with $H^j(E_n)=0$ for $j>n$ and colimit legs inducing isomorphisms for $j\le n$; allow isomorphic presentations. Apply [lem-trf-truncation-colimit-resolving-cover] to each complex $K$. Its $E$, colimit legs and quasi-isomorphism $a:E\to K$ show that every $K$ receives a quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal R$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph and definition of the class in the claim.

proof.text: For any quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:X\to Y$ with $X,Y\in\mathcal R$, choose witnessing towers. If a presentation is given up to an isomorphism, compose its legs with that isomorphism; the colimit universal property and the cohomology conditions are preserved. All hypotheses of [lem-trf-resolution-colimit-quasi-isos] hold: the original bounded-above acyclicity hypothesis is on $\mathcal P$, the towers have terms in its isomorphism closure, $F$ preserves sequential colimits, and these colimits are exact in $\mathcal B$. Thus $F(\alpha)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $Q_{\mathcal B}K(F)$ inverts this arrow.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, claim and final paragraph.

proof.text: Additivity identifies $F(K[1])$ with $F(K)[1]$ and sends the cone matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ to $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}F(d_L)&F(f)\\0&-F(d_K)\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Hence $K(F)$ preserves cone triangles and is exact. By [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated], $Q_{\mathcal B}$ is exact and quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A)$ have the fraction calculus, two-out-of-three and triangulated compatibility. Thus $Q_{\mathcal B}K(F)$ has the setup of Situation 05S8. The identity $F(dh+hd)=F(d)F(h)+F(h)F(d)$ also shows that termwise application descends to homotopy classes.

source.place: Tag 0794, reduction to Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes; Situation 05S8.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy] with $C=K(\mathcal A)$, $W$ the quasi-isomorphisms, $H=D(\mathcal B)$, functor $Q_{\mathcal B}K(F)$ and class $\mathcal R$. Use the images in $K(\mathcal A)$ of the complexes of $\mathcal R$. Every $W$-arrow between them has a quasi-isomorphism of complexes as representative, to which step 2 applies. Steps 1 and 2 give its resolution and inversion hypotheses; step 3 gives its fraction hypotheses. It makes every denominator diagram $W/K\to D(\mathcal B)$ essentially constant. By [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], this is precisely that the left derived functor is defined at each $K$.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual assertion; Tag 0794 conclusion and Definition 05S9.
